rationale: This cross-sectional observational study surveys 160 households across 16 randomly selected rural water supply systems in Achefer, Ethiopia, using Tobit censored regressions to test determinants of household management contributions. The central institutional mechanisms tested as explanatory exposures belong to participation_assistance: degree of household participation during project design and implementation (DPARDPIMP), trust in village water use committees (TOWUCs), and project health/management advocacy (ADVOCACY), alongside contextual discussion of WUC-set monthly tariffs/cost-recovery rules (fees_tariffs_subsidies). The empirical dependent variables are household cash contributions (CASHCONT) and labour contributions (LABORCONT) toward WUC operation and maintenance (plus aggregate O&M cost-coverage adequacy at 19%), which represent institutional/governance intermediate and contribution-compliance outcomes (administrative_outcome) rather than direct empirical outcomes of physical connection or service functionality.
